images.caption: Members of the public queue outside St. Stephen's entrance waiting to view the lying in state of King Edward VII. The King had died at Sandringham on 6th May 1910 after a series of heart attacks, he lay in state firstly at Buckingham Palace and then in Westminster Hall on the 17th, 18th and 19th May. The funeral took place the next day on the 20th May at Windsor. An unusually clear photograph for the time except for the section on the right.
images.alt: Members of the public queue outside St. Stephen's entrance waiting to view the lying in state of King Edward VII. images.caption:
For me the interesting part of the photograph is the building work taking place in Millbank. Most of this north part of Millbank is owned by the Church Commissioners and the building under construction is the office of the Crown agents which was begun in 1912, so this may be 1912/13.

The area which was to become Victoria Tower Gardens is still occupied by wharves and Industrial units, the area was cleared by 1915.
